thread:
maria: heads-up — noticed a drop in prefix cache hits for hosted region eu-west-1 starting ~04:10 UTC, looks correlated with yesterday's runtime kernel-selector roll
jun: are we seeing the same on dedicated/private? quick numbers?
sasha: hosted hit-rate ~68% -> 47% after rollout. dedicated stayed ~92%. private in customer VPCs dropped to ~54% but higher variance.
kevin: uh, big delta. any change to keying or salt in the rollout?
maria: kernel-selector 3.2 changed some op ordering; also we changed a cache key normalization tweak (lowercasing + whitespace trim) but the rollout only targeted hosted.
jun: interesting — if normalization changed, keys could diverge between deployments. but why dedicated unaffected?
sasha: dedicated uses local SSD netstore for KV; hosted uses s3-backed netstore behind proxy with 30-50ms variance. private customers on NFS have higher path length + own KMS.
kevin: maybe warmup strategy interacts with batching heuristics. More batching -> fewer unique prefixes observed -> slower spreading of cache entries across shards.
maria: telemetry dump (excerpt):
```
region    before_hit   after_hit   sample_size
hosted-eu 0.68         0.47        1.2M
dedicated  0.92         0.91        0.4M
private    0.56         0.54        0.2M
```
jun: can we reproduce locally by toggling netstore latency + kernel-selector? I'll spin up a sim.
kevin: quick check — ops trace shows more cache-misses had mismatch in `prompt_key` length and an extra trailing null in hosted logs. so maybe serialization change in the proxy layer.
sasha: that points to a regression in proxy serialization or the normalization change you mentioned. hosted got both the kernel update and proxy patch in same window.
maria: hypothesis: two orthogonal changes — 1) normalization tweak changed canonical keys, 2) kernel-selector changed batching shape so fewer prefix reuse during warmup; together they amplified miss rate on hosted where netstore lookups are more expensive -> cascade effect.
jun: plan:
- revert normalization in hosted as a canary
- add instrumentation to compare raw vs normalized key counts
- run targeted warmup: staggered prefix replay to populate cache shards
- add a serialization compatibility test in proxy CI
kevin: SG. I can patch a canary with normalization off and enable extra logging for `prompt_key` diffs.
sasha: I'll prepare a short load driver that replays the top 50 prefixes with different batch sizes to see warmup sensitivity. use `--batch-size 8/16/32`.
maria: sample command for the replay driver:
```
./replay --region eu-west-1 --prefix-file top50.txt --rate 200/s --batch-size 16
```
jun: timeline? if canary looks good we can rollback the kernel-selector only if needed. otherwise we might need to implement compatibility layer in proxy.
kevin: giving this priority — will flip canary 10:20 UTC and monitor `cache.hit_rate` and p95 latency.
perf-bot: deploy-log: canary deploy started by kevin at 10:21 UTC -> target: hosted-eu hostpool-3
maria: thanks. if this is indeed a key serialization mismatch we should also add a migration step to re-normalize existing keys in netstore to avoid prolonged cold misses.
jun: agree. also add a metric `key-equiv-entropy` to detect salt/normalization drift across deployments.
kevin: noted. I'll post results in ~30m.
perf-bot: metric-alert resolved: spike in cache-miss-rate cleared at 10:43 UTC (post-canary). :tada:
maria: can confirm hosted hit-rate back to ~70% after canary and staggered warmup. follow-ups: PR for proxy serialization tests, add rollout guard to require keying-compat flag, and a short runbook for future mixed-rollouts.
sasha: adding those to the eng-runtime backlog now.
jun: awesome work team. :thumbsup:
